content.title: FOODS FOR ORGANS {{NOBODY}} EVER TALKS ABOUT
facts: **Beets** are good for BLOOD VESSELS – the nitrates relax and widen them, helping blood flow easier so your heart doesn't have to work as hard.
**Sardines** are good for BONE MARROW – tiny edible bones deliver calcium and vitamin D right where new blood cells are made.
**Pumpkin seeds** are good for the BLADDER – 1 oz/day gives you magnesium and zinc that support normal bladder muscle function.
**Blueberries** are good for the HIPPOCAMPUS – compounds called anthocyanins cross into brain tissue and support memory-related regions.
**Oats** are good for the GUT LINING – the beta-glucan fiber forms a gel that feeds the mucus layer protecting your intestinal wall.
**Walnuts** are good for the RETINA – 1 small handful/day supplies omega-3s that are structural fats found in the eye's light-sensing cells.
**Dark chocolate (70%+)** is good for the INNER EAR – flavanols support tiny blood vessels that feed the structures responsible for balance.
**Lentils** are good for the SPLEEN – slow-releasing iron helps replenish red blood cells that the spleen filters daily.

caption:
Some of the most useful foods never get mentioned because the organs they support don't get much airtime. Beets deserve more credit than they get — the nitrates they contain get converted into nitric oxide in your body, which is the same molecule your blood vessels use to signal 'relax and open up,' easing overall circulation. Pumpkin seeds are another quiet hero: the magnesium and zinc inside them play a role in how nerve signals fire to your bladder muscle, which is part of why they're often mentioned for urinary comfort. And walnuts are worth a second look too — the omega-3 fat they provide (called ALA) gets incorporated into cell membranes in the retina, the part of your eye that actually processes light into images. Everyone's body is different, so treat these as gentle additions, not fixes.
